== 7b3m-3o5XYw The One Thing Every Aluminum Boat Owner Should Do | Alaska
I hadn't been down to the boat in almost a month. When a buddy needed a load of building materials hauled across Kachemak Bay, it was the perfect excuse to get back on the water and check everything over. / First thing — fire up the heater, because it's October in Alaska. Then I opened up the voids below deck. If you own an aluminum boat, this part's for you. My boat is starting to show some corrosion in the bottom plating, and I learned something I didn't know before: the anodes on the outside of your hull only protect the outside. Water that sits inside a void — mostly from condensation — becomes its own electrolyte, and nothing is protecting it. The fix that's working for me is simple: keep it bone dry with bentonite clay desiccant bags, and check them regularly. / Then we loaded up on a rising tide and headed across the bay.
